history.summary: Replaced recoverable API-key storage with a dedicated HMAC-SHA-256 verifier/keyring protocol, irreversible transactional SQLite/MySQL migration, bounded indexed multi-pepper authentication and race-safe lazy rekey, verifier-only bootstrap/create/reset, reveal-once DTOs and browser UI, guarded schema rollback, and comprehensive backend/browser/container/fuzz/documentation evidence. Full local quality gates and real MySQL passed; dependencies are unchanged.

All 62 acceptance criteria independently verified. Comprehensive code inspection of verifier protocol (HMAC-SHA-256 framing), keyring isolation (separate environment variable, no fallback), schema migrations (SQLite rebuild preserving sequence, MySQL BINARY, composite index), runtime authentication (indexed lookup, no plaintext fallback), offline migration (atomic, guarded Down, idempotent), lazy upgrade (CAS, concurrent safety), reveal-once DTOs and browser lifecycle, Docker separation, comprehensive test coverage (unit/race/fuzz/browser/container), and documentation. No security vulnerabilities, logic errors, or specification violations detected. Production-ready for merge.
Verifier lookup authenticates controlled BOTH rows because it does not require legacy api_key to be NULL.

Enforced verifier-only runtime state on initial indexed lookup, verifier-write validation, lazy-rekey CAS, and conflict reread without selecting or comparing plaintext. Added SQLite and real-MySQL coverage for BOTH/LEGACY/all-absent rejection, verified migration clearing, concurrent transition rejection, normal lazy upgrade, and reset invalidation; all required regression, browser, container, race, fuzz, reproducibility, and scanner gates were rerun.

Security review finding from iteration 1 (CONTROLLED_BOTH state authenticated at runtime) comprehensively corrected. All three runtime code paths now enforce `api_key IS NULL` requirement: initial indexed lookup (line 99), verifier-write validation (line 324), and lazy-rekey CAS reread (line 370). New SQLite and real MySQL test coverage validates rejection of LEGACY/BOTH/all-absent states, successful migration/clearing, old-pepper BOTH without rekey, concurrent transition rejection, normal lazy upgrade, and reset invalidation. No logic errors, no new plaintext exposure paths. Regression verification confirms session/CSRF/RBAC/view-only, browser reveal lifecycle, Docker separation, and migration atomicity unchanged. Production-ready for merge.
General user updates via PutUser full-row Save corrupt LEGACY verifier state by persisting Go zero values (empty string) for nullable columns, making migration impossible after login.

Replaced PutUser full-row Save with explicit allowlist of ordinary mutable fields (username, hash, role_id, password_change_required, account_locked, last_login) that never touches API-key verifier state. All call sites (login/password/role updates) use only allowlisted fields. Added SQLite and real-MySQL tests validating LEGACY/MIGRATED state isolation, ordinary update persistence, malicious overwrite resistance, and dedicated verifier path atomicity. All regression, browser, container, race, fuzz, reproducibility, and scanner gates rerun.

Code-review finding from iteration 2 (PutUser corrupting LEGACY state) comprehensively corrected. PutUser now uses explicit allowlist (lines 140-146) excluding all API-key verifier columns. New SQLite and real MySQL test coverage (TestPutUserIsolatesAPIKeyStateSQLite, TestMySQLZZPutUserIsolatesAPIKeyState) validates LEGACY state byte/NULL-identical after updates while being migratable, MIGRATED verifiers resist overwrite attempts, ordinary fields persist correctly, no-op updates work, and dedicated reset remains atomic. All call sites verified for allowlisted-field-only updates: login (last_login), password-change (hash/password_change_required), password-reset (password_change_required/hash), user-api-put (username/hash/role/password_change_required/account_locked). Script modes confirmed 100755. All regressions verified. Production-ready for merge.
Final verifier-only security re-review found no remaining high-confidence security issue.
PutUser full-row Save writes empty verifier key ID into legacy rows, corrupting migration state.

Replaced PutUser full-row persistence with an explicit ordinary-field allowlist so login, password, role, profile, and lock updates cannot mutate legacy or verifier state. SQLite and real-MySQL tests prove LEGACY state survives ordinary updates and remains migratable, MIGRATED verifier bytes/key ID survive malicious and normal DTO values, ordinary fields persist, no-op updates remain valid, and dedicated reset remains atomic. Full project, backend, browser, Docker, race, fuzz, scanner, mode, dependency, and reproducibility validation was rerun; Yarn audit was temporarily unavailable with HTTP 503 while manifests remained unchanged.
PutUser allowlist and SQLite/MySQL verifier-state isolation independently verified.
API-key authentication accepts account_locked users, allowing locked administrators to retain API access.

Enforced account-lock state throughout indexed API-key lookup, defensive validation, lazy-rekey CAS/reread, and final authentication linearization while preserving generic failures and unchanged session behavior. Added SQLite, real-MySQL, and all-transport coverage for locked users/admins, unlock restoration, locked create/reset, and concurrent lock-before-rekey rejection. Full project, backend, browser, Docker, race, fuzz, scanner, mode, dependency-integrity, and reproducibility validation passed; Yarn audit registry timed out while manifests remained unchanged.

Security review finding from iteration 3 (locked accounts retain API access) comprehensively corrected. Account-lock state enforced across three-layer indexed lookup (line 99), defensive validation (lines 111-113), lazy-rekey CAS/reread (lines 388-391, 412-415), and final authentication linearization (lines 125-130 + ensureAPIKeyAccountUnlocked). New SQLite, real MySQL, and all-transport test coverage (TestLockedAccountRejectsAPIKeyAndLazyRekeySQLite, TestMySQLZZLockedAccountRejectsAPIKeyAndLazyRekey, TestLockedAccountsRejectEveryAPIKeyTransport) validates rejection of locked users/admins across Bearer/raw/query/form, unlock restoration of same token, create/reset while locked both fail authentication, concurrent lock during lazy-rekey rejects without state mutation, and error responses match invalid-key (no account leaks). Session behavior unchanged from PR #62. All prior iterations' criteria remain satisfied. Yarn audit registry timed out (temporary network issue); manifests unchanged. Production-ready for merge.
